page: Microsoft Azure D32pls_v5 is a compute-oriented virtual machine within the Dplsv5 series, utilizing the 64-bit ARM architecture. Powered by Ampere Neoverse-N1 processors operating at a sustained clock speed of 3.0 GHz, the instance supplies 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped directly to 32 physical cores with single-threaded execution. System resources include 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per core). Local disk storage is not bundled with this instance type, requiring external remote block storage via Azure Premium Storage for persistent workloads, and it includes no integrated hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate dependable multi-threaded throughput balanced against modest single-thread execution rates. In PassMark CPU evaluation, the instance achieved a multi-core score of 20,154.2 alongside 57,267.23 in stress-ng multi-core testing. Geekbench testing mirrors this profile, yielding an average multi-core score of 12,640.0 against a weaker single-core rating of 1,100.0, driven by the IPC profile of the Neoverse-N1 architecture. Memory subsystems provide robust uncached large-block bandwidth, achieving 170.47 GB/sec read and 77.32 GB/sec write throughput. While small model inference functions capably, large-model execution (70B) yields weak performance due to limited memory capacity and absent GPU acceleration.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the D32pls_v5 presents strong multi-threaded resource density for horizontally scalable workloads. The single thread-per-core topology avoids hyperthreading contention, delivering predictable execution behavior across sustained batch jobs. However, software stacks must support native arm64 instructions, and the lower memory allotment per core limits dense in-memory caching profiles.

This server type is primarily suited for scale-out compute tasks, multi-threaded microservices, Clang-based software compilation pipelines, static web serving infrastructure, and containerized application deployments.

Equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It incorporates no onboard local storage or GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage options. Performance benchmarks reveal consistent multi-threaded computational power, highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 20,154.2 and stress-ng multi-core score of 57,267.23, although single-core metrics remain modest. The 32-core dedicated topology eliminates hyperthreading interference, making it cost-efficient for horizontal scaling. This instance is well tailored for multi-threaded compilation tasks, static web serving, containerized services, and distributed microservices adapted for ARM64.
